title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Admitting Guilt - False Alibi
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client charged with Careless Driving privately admits to the paralegal that they were driving the car and caused the accident. The client then instructs the paralegal: "I want to take the stand and testify that my sister was driving the car." What is the paralegal's mandatory ethical duty?
options: Allow the client to testify, as it is the client's constitutional right to make a full answer and defence.
Refuse to allow the client to give this testimony, as it is perjury. If the client insists, the paralegal must withdraw.
Let the client testify, but secretly signal to the prosecutor that the client is lying.
Refuse to let the client testify, but suggest the sister come in and falsely confess instead.
questions.explain: While a paralegal can represent an admitted-guilty client who pleads not guilty (by simply testing the Crown's evidence), the paralegal is strictly forbidden from suborning perjury or setting up a false alibi. If the client insists on committing perjury, the paralegal must withdraw (Mandatory Withdrawal under Rule 8.02).
